q: The SI unit of moment of inertia is
why: I = sum(m r^2), units kg x m^2

q: Radius of gyration K is related to moment of inertia I and mass M by
why: By definition I = M K^2, so K = sqrt(I/M)

q: A ring of mass 2 kg and radius 0.5 m rotates about its central axis. Its moment of inertia is
According to the theorem of parallel axes, if Ic is the moment of inertia about an axis through the centre of mass, the moment of inertia about a parallel axis at distance h is
why: Parallel axis theorem: I = Ic + M h^2

q: The theorem of perpendicular axes applies to
why: This theorem is valid only for plane (two-dimensional) laminar bodies

q: According to the theorem of perpendicular axes, Iz for a lamina equals
why: Iz = Ix + Iy, where x and y axes lie in the plane of the lamina

q: The angular momentum L of a rotating body is given by
why: Angular momentum L = I omega, analogous to p = mv

q: If no external torque acts on a rotating system, then
o: moment of inertia is always constant
why: Conservation of angular momentum: when torque = 0, I omega stays constant, so I1 omega1 = I2 omega2

q: A car moving on a banked road without tendency to skid satisfies
why: Banking condition: tan theta = v^2 / (r g)

q: The maximum safe speed on a banked curve of radius r and banking angle theta is
why: From tan theta = v^2/(rg), v = sqrt(r g tan theta)
